content:
For seven years, Jay-Z has been the man behind the Super Bowl halftime show. On February 14, 2027, he will finally be the man on its stage. The NFL, Apple Music and Roc Nation announced Monday, October 26, that the 25-time Grammy winner will headline the Apple Music Super Bowl LXI Halftime Show at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

The announcement came at the start of halftime during Monday Night Football's matchup between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Dallas Cowboys. The game will air on ESPN, ABC and Disney+, with mobile streaming available through NFL+.

The booking closes a circle that began in 2019, when Roc Nation, Jay-Z's entertainment company, partnered with the NFL to produce the halftime show and advise on league music events. Since then, Jay-Z has helped select the performers for football's biggest stage, including Rihanna, Usher, Kendrick Lamar and Bad Bunny, while remaining behind the scenes himself.

NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said a Jay-Z headline set had been his request from the start. "When we first reached an agreement with Roc Nation to produce the show, I had just one request: that Jay-Z take the stage himself one day, whenever the moment felt right to him," Goodell said. "I couldn't be more excited for fans around the world to experience the artistry, creativity and cultural impact he will bring to the Super Bowl stage."

Jay-Z, whose real name is Shawn Carter, framed the moment as the capstone of a 30-year run. "From Reasonable Doubt to standing on the Super Bowl Halftime stage, this has been a journey," he said in a statement. "Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world's biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true."

The timing is no accident. This year marks the 30th anniversary of his debut album, Reasonable Doubt. Over the prior weekend, Jay-Z wrapped his "Jay-Z 30" concert series with two shows on October 23 and 24 at the very same SoFi Stadium where he will perform in February, with onstage guests including John Legend, DJ Khaled, Snoop Dogg, Dr. Dre and his daughter Blue Ivy Carter. The announcement teaser leaned into the joke, showing him surrounded by goats under the tagline "GOAT's out of the bag."

The history gives the booking an edge other halftime announcements do not carry. Jay-Z rapped about turning down a Super Bowl invitation on The Carters' 2018 track "APESHIT," a stance widely linked to his support for Colin Kaepernick. Eight years later, he is stepping onto the stage his own company helped rebuild.

Analysis: The Curator Cashes In His Own Credibility

This is not just another big-name halftime booking; it is the NFL letting its own tastemaker take the stage he built. Jay-Z spent seven years lending the halftime show credibility with artists who defined their eras, and now that credibility transfers to him in a single night. The risk is the obvious one, and it is the reason the announcement landed with a question attached: did the man who picks the performer just pick himself? The answer, on the record, is that Goodell asked for this from day one. But the show in February will be judged on a harder standard than any previous halftime set, because the audience knows exactly who assembled it. If it lands, it cements a 30-year career as the defining arc of modern halftime history. If it does not, the curator will have no one to blame but the mirror.

title: The Curator Takes the Stage: Jay-Z to Headline the 2027 Super Bowl Halftime Show
